Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 50, English)
The Dimension ( ड ाय म ेंश न) Concept: How Bhakti, Birth, and Guru Shape Your Astral "Floor"

Sour ce: a Mool T atva live session opening with hawan-scheduling clarifications, then an extended teaching on the "Dimension" concept — what it is, how it is measur ed, how it rises and falls, and why choosing a guru is one of the most consequential decisions a practitioner can make.
1. Which Hawan Should You Attend?

Bhaiya opens by addressing a recurring question — which hawan should a given person register for? He points people back to Ashaeiynn's original 15-minute "Mool Tatva" introduction video, which explains the basic structure: Mahayagya happens once a month, on Purnima (full moon) , while the daily hawan handles negativity . Crucially , Mahayagya itself is not for negativity — it carries a separate sankalp (resolve) whose sole purpose is to increase a person's bhakti tatva (devotion element).
2. Bhakti vs. Shakti: The Missing Half of Every Spiritual Conversation

Bhaiya observes that wherever you go, whichever tradition or tatva you study , people will talk to you about shakti (power) and sadhna (practice) — but almost no one talks about bhakti (devotion). Yet, per this teaching, without bhakti a human being cannot attain shakti at all — in truth, bhakti itself is the most complete form of shakti, but people don't accept this. Translated into astral-world terms, bhakti corr esponds to a person's "Dimension."
3. What "Dimension" Means

"Dimension" is explicitly a word Bhaiya coined himself — his guru gave him a Sanskrit term for the concept that didn't stick in his understanding, so he substituted a simpler word. Dimension is the element that decides a person's "jagriti skeleton" — i.e., the foundational framework of a person's spiritual/karmic standing. It is present in every human being from birth and shapes physical form, attraction, manner of speech, what one eats and drinks, how much money and status one gets, and whose voice carries weight in a room.
4. The Chakra-to-Dimension Mapping

Per this teaching, everyone knows about the seven classical chakras. What is less known: above these seven chakras lie seven mor e chakras (14 total). Crossing all 14 and passing beyond a kind of astral "sky" constitutes the first Dimension . The next Dimension directly after that is the 32-chakra Dimension . The relationship is explained with an analogy: chakras ar e like stairs (steps); Dimensions ar e like floors.
5. Climbing Floors Doesn't Make You King of Them

Reaching a new floor (Dimension) does not mean you rule it. Each floor already has many subtle bodies ( सूक्ष्म शरीर ) residing there — people just like you who must also be "crossed" before advancing further . Dimension is thus a layer ed hierar chy of subtle beings, not
a single leap to power .
6. Dimension Is Independent of Bhakti

A person who does no devotional practice at all still has a Dimension — Dimension exists worldwide for every human, devotee or not, because physical-world Dimension and astral-world Dimension ar e separate tracks. Someone with a strong astral Dimension effectively behaves like royalty in the unseen world even without visible spiritual achievement — illustrated with examples of a famous Italian singer (roughly 7 crore Dimension) and a Turkish television actress (roughly 14 crore Dimension), neither of whom has any conscious awareness of the concept.
7. The Measuring Scale and Personal Case Studies

Bhaiya's guru gave him a numeric scale for measuring Dimension (analogous to how scientists use light-years for planets or feet/inches for physical objects) so there would be a common reference point. On this scale, ordinary people are commonly found anywhere from roughly 500 up to 5,000–8,000.

Bhaiya recounts checking his own Dimension against a childhood classmate nicknamed "Poli" (V eeresh Angras, from a family of rishis). At birth, Bhaiya's own Dimension was roughly 33,000 — but due to sustained tantric attacks tar geting him (originating from displaced anger in his own family , discussed further below), it had fallen to zero, then into negative territory , confirmed independently when Ankur Bhaiya also checked and saw "minus." Meanwhile, Poli's own birth Dimension was checked at 2.5 cr or e, though by the time Bhaiya checked him years later it had fallen to around 500 — still roughly 500 times higher than Bhaiya's own zero at that time.
8. Why Dimension Fell: Displaced Family Anger

Investigating why his own Dimension had collapsed, Bhaiya discovered that unresolved anger and jealousy directed at his father and mother by others was, in ef fect, dischar ged onto him as a child — a mechanism by which a family member's negativity gets inherited by the next generation without any personal wrongdoing on the child's part.
9. Dimension as the Chain Linking Birth to Birth

Bhaiya's guru's core teaching on this subject: "Dimension is the link that connects one birth to the next." It decides what a person will become, which birth they will take, and how their life will unfold. This teaching states Dimension functions as the exact measuring chart that devtas use to judge a person's "aukaat" (worth/standing).
10. No One Can Stand Still on a Dimension

A critical rule: a person cannot r emain static on any given Dimension. If you believe you've reached, say , one crore Dimension and can now relax, you cannot — because subtle bodies already stationed at that level will contest you daily and pull you back down if you stop advancing. You either keep climbing, or you begin falling from wherever you stopped.
1 1. Only Humans Can Lower a Human's Dimension

Per this teaching, this is one of the most important — and startling — rules Bhaiya's guru revealed: Bhagwan and devtas never interfere with a person's Dimension. Only another human being can lower (or , implicitly , help raise) another human's Dimension. Bhaiya describes being genuinely shocked when he first learned this.
12. Raising Dimension: Physical and Astral Paths

Dimension can be raised through physical means — yoga, exercise, surya namaskar , pranic healing, and quality food and drink (this teaching notes that every object has its own Dimension, illustrated by comparing a OnePlus phone, an iPhone, and a Samsung phone as
each carrying a dif ferent Dimension) — or through astral means , namely dhyan (meditation), tap (austerity), and mantra jaap.
13. Mantra Dimension vs. Personal Dimension

A pivotal realization in Bhaiya's own journey: even while his personal Dimension sat at zero or in negative territory , his mantra's Dimension was already in the "kharabs" (hundreds of billions) — because the mantra shakti given to him was already jagrit (awakened) from the start. This is why , per this teaching, 33 tantriks who attacked him over the years all ended up with their siddhis rendered inef fective ("gili" / wet) — they were contending with his mantra's Dimension, not his own personal one.
14. Why Personal Dimension Still Matters

Even with an enormously high mantra Dimension, this teaching states a person still needs to raise their own personal Dimension eventually — because recognition and standing among fellow humans ( मान्यता) requires rising within the shared human tatva that exists in everyone. Mantra Dimension and personal Dimension are related but distinct tracks, and both matter .
15. Recovering Lost Gr ound

Once Bhaiya understood the Dimension concept, he "reclaimed" roughly 90,000 Dimension retroactively , corresponding to all the japa/practice he had already done before fully grasping the concept — after which continued Jai Siyaram jaap kept compounding the gain. He notes that photos of himself from five years earlier versus now show a visible physical dif ference tied to this rise.
16. Everyday Examples of Dimension Rising and Falling — With or Without Bhakti

Dimension can rise even without conscious devotional practice, through consistently maintained principled behavior — but per this teaching, each such practice has its own ceiling. Punctuality alone might carry a person to a Dimension somewhere between 10,000 and 30,000 over a 50-year span, and no further; a habit like always eating a healthy breakfast, or always sleeping and waking on a fixed schedule (the teaching references Akshay Kumar's early-rising discipline as an example), each caps out at its own particular ceiling.

This is illustrated by contrasting Akshay Kumar (extremely disciplined, punctual, fit) with Shah Rukh Khan: Akshay's discipline alone caps his Dimension at a certain point that discipline cannot exceed, while a person who has instead anchored themselves to an external shakti (devotional or otherwise) is not bound by that same ceiling.

A cautionary anecdote: Akshay Kumar is described as having, some years ago, reasoned that the cost of visiting Vaishno Devi (flights, helicopter , of ferings) would be better spent on more "practical" things like clothing — and per this teaching, that rationalization itself corresponded to a real loss of Dimension, illustrating that discounting devotional practice for seemingly sensible practical reasons carries a real spiritual cost.

The key rule stated plainly: a person can never rise above the particular ceiling set by whatever specific non-devotional practice they r ely on — only anchoring to an external shakti in sustained, r epeated devotion can carry a person beyond any such ceiling.
17. The Highest Dimension: Mahadev

Investigating who holds the highest Dimension of all, Bhaiya's search led to Mahadev (Shiva) — and since this teaching states the Dimension concept applies specifically to humans (not to Bhagwan Ram, who is explicitly placed outside this framework), the implication drawn is that Mahadev himself was, at some point, human. The relative dif ference between Devi Maa's and Mahadev's respective Dimensions is deliberately deferred to a separate, dedicated Kuldevta session for another day .
18. Even One's Own Guru Has a Dimension

Continuing the same search, Bhaiya found that his own guru, Hanuman Ji Maharaj, also has a Dimension — vastly smaller than Mahadev's, but still enormous. The reasoning that follows: since a guru already possesses a lar ge Dimension, that guru can carry a
devoted disciple upward along with him.
19. The Danger of Making Any Human Body Your Guru

This teaching gives an extended, direct warning about human gurus: if you make any living human being your guru, your own Dimension can never exceed that guru's Dimension for as long as that person remains your guru. Worse — if that guru's Dimension ever falls (through a tantric attack, personal moral failing, or even losing their sanity), your Dimension falls with it , because that person is the one responsible for raising you in the first place. Bhaiya states this is precisely why a person should think "a thousand, a lakh, a crore, a kharab times" before making any human body their guru.
20. The Alternative: A "Jeevit Samadhi" Guru

The teaching's recommended alternative: a guru who has taken Jeevit Samadhi (living samadhi) — meaning they are fully , permanently jagrit. Such beings (the teaching names Neem Karoli Baba as an example) continue gr owing their own Dimension without limit, indefinitely , unlike an ordinary living human teacher whose Dimension is fixed to their mortal, fallible state. All devidevatas, per this teaching, are likewise continuously growing their own Dimension without end — and Mahadev is described as advancing "like a missile," answerable to no one.

Bhaiya of fers a lighter alternative to formal guru-disciple relationships with ordinary humans: treat each other as brothers/companions in devotion rather than guru and disciple — walking the path together , praying for one another , without the binding risk a formal human guru relationship carries.
21. Devtas Never Fight Over Dimension Disputes

Per this teaching, devtas never intervene in Dimension-based conflicts between two devotees of the same deity . Even in a hypothetical clash between two well-known dhams devoted to the same deity , that deity would never take sides, because such disputes are purely human matters of tapobal (austerity-power), mantra shakti, tap shakti, and kundli shakti — devtas simply do not enter Dimension warfare.
22. How Prayer Still Helps When Your Guru's Tatva Is Pr esent at Every Level Below Him

Despite devtas staying out of Dimension disputes, a devotee is not defenseless: because a guru's own tatva (essence) is present at every Dimension level below the guru's own maximum, a sincere prayer invoking the guru can activate that guru's subtle presence at the exact level of an attacker , correcting the imbalance — but only if the guru's own Dimension is genuinely high enough to reach that level in the first place. If your chosen guru's own Dimension is too low , your prayer simply cannot "reach" far enough to help you, reinforcing the earlier warning about the risk of a low-Dimension human guru.
23. Case Study: The "Anshu" Household Pattern

Bhaiya illustrates how repeated ritual action by a well-meaning but unaware family member can create an unintended protective/negative cycle: a mother , worried about controlling her son ("Anshu"), consults a pandit and is told to perform a specific ritual daily without fail. Because Anshu himself has, knowingly or not, granted his mother a form of blessing/shakti, that shakti now stands behind her and empowers her daily ritual, regardless of her own lack of awareness of what she's doing.

If a tantrik or any external force tries to attack Anshu directly , they cannot — his own power protects him, and it also protects his innocent, unaware mother (since she acted only out of devotion, not from Anshu's malicious intent). Per this teaching, in such cases the attacking action is declar ed "null and void" — it produces no real ef fect on Anshu at all. The only real resolution in such a cycle is for the tar geted person (Anshu, or anyone in a similar situation) to raise their own personal Dimension , so that repeating rituals or cycles around them lose their capacity to af fect them at all.
24. Why Ashaeiynn's Mahayagya Exists

It took Bhaiya roughly a full year to understand why a dedicated collective ritual was needed for people who could not raise their own Dimension through personal ef fort alone. This led to the creation of Mahayagya , held once monthly on Purnima, whose specific sankalp is to work directly on raising participants' Dimension — supplementing what any individual practitioner could achieve alone. A single Mahayagya session can raise a participant's Dimension by roughly 50 to 500 points.
25. Two Parallel Sankalps: Jagriti and Raksha Suraksha

Beyond the Dimension-raising Jagriti Bhakti sankalp performed each Purnima, Ashaeiynn also runs a second, ongoing sankalp called Raksha Suraksha (protection/security) — intended specifically for people whose devotional practice is being actively obstructed by someone close to them (a family member who won't "let them" do jaap, for instance). Raising one's own Dimension via this sankalp effectively brings the obstructing party "below" the practitioner , so that person becomes receptive to what the practitioner asks of them.
26. Why Dimension Gains Compound Rather Than Add Up Linearly

Responding to a sangat member's skeptical, math-based question (whether years of practice could realistically explain the scale of gains observed), Bhaiya clarifies that Dimension gains are not additive but exponential/compounding. An 1 1-hour jaap session might raise Dimension by roughly 50 points on its own — but that same session also grows the practitioner's underlying mantra shakti, which itself carries its own (much lar ger) Dimension. Because mantra-shakti Dimension compounds together with personal Dimension gains across repeated sessions, the total result multiplies rather than simply accumulating — illustrated with a projection of roughly 5 crore Dimension after approximately 1,000 cumulative hours of practice, far beyond what simple multiplication of a flat 50-points-per - session rate would suggest.
27. Why Mahayagya Gains Also Compound

The same compounding logic explains why participants' Dimension gains from Ashaeiynn's ten Mahayagyas held to date (over ten months) far exceed a naive linear estimate (which would suggest only about 25,000 total Dimension gained). Each Mahayagya not only grants a direct 50–500 point Dimension gift but also strengthens the participant's ongoing mantra shakti and their bond with fellow sadhaks/saints, so subsequent sessions build on genuinely compounded prior gains rather than starting fresh each time.
28. Why Mahayagya Slots Still Include Pitru and Negativity Categories

Closing the session, Bhaiya clarifies a practical registration question: even though Mahayagya's core sankalp is Jagriti/Dimensionraising and Raksha Suraksha, pitru and negativity hawan ar e still performed daily as part of the ordinary r outine , and on Mahayagya day specifically , the much lar ger quantity of bhog of fered draws a correspondingly lar ger number of saints and mahatmas — compressing roughly ten days' worth of ordinary pitru/negativity clearing work into a single day's Mahayagya session.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Dimension = the astral-world measur e of bhakti tatva — devtas' own "measuring chart" of a person's standing, distinct from mantra Dimension. Dimension is built from 14 chakras = 1st Dimension , next 32 chakras = 2nd Dimension ; chakras are steps, Dimensions are floors. Only humans lower (or raise) a human's Dimension — Bhagwan and devtas never interfere in Dimension matters, including disputes between two devotees of the same deity . No one can stand still on a Dimension — you either keep climbing or start falling from wherever you stop. Dimension can rise via physical means (yoga, exercise, food/quality of possessions) or astral means (dhyan, tap, mantra jaap) — but purely disciplined/non-devotional practices each have their own fixed ceiling.

Mantra Dimension and personal Dimension ar e separate tracks — a hugely jagrit mantra can protect a practitioner even while their personal Dimension is low , but personal Dimension is still needed for human-world recognition. Never make a living human body your guru without extr eme caution — your Dimension is capped at theirs, and falls if theirs falls; prefer a "Jeevit Samadhi" guru whose Dimension grows without limit. A guru's tatva is present at every Dimension level below the guru's own — prayer can invoke that presence to help you, but only as far as the guru's own Dimension genuinely reaches. Repeated rituals performed unknowingly by an innocent family member on a protected person's behalf can render outside attacks "null and void" — but the real fix is the protected person raising their own Dimension. Mahayagya's Jagriti sankalp exists specifically to raise Dimension (50–500 points per session) for those who cannot raise it through personal ef fort alone; Raksha Suraksha sankalp exists for those being actively obstructed from practicing. Dimension gains compound exponentially , not linearly — mantra shakti's own growing Dimension multiplies personal gains across repeated sessions. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 50, English)
The Dimension ( ड ाय म ेंश न) Concept: How Bhakti, Birth, and Guru Shape Your Astral "Floor"
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. How do I know which hawan I should attend — the daily one or the monthly Mahayagya? A: Per this teaching, the daily hawan is specifically for handling negativity , while Mahayagya happens once a month on Purnima and is not for negativity at all — it carries a separate sankalp whose sole purpose is increasing a person's bhakti tatva (devotion element). Watching Ashaeiynn's original 15-minute "Mool Tatva" introduction video covers this distinction clearly .

Q2. Why does almost no spiritual teaching talk about bhakti, only about shakti and sadhna? A: This teaching states that's simply an observed gap — nearly every tradition emphasizes power and practice, but in truth, bhakti (devotion) is itself the most complete form of shakti; a human being cannot attain real shakti without it.

Q3. What exactly is "Dimension" in this teaching's framework? A: Dimension is a word Bhaiya coined himself (his guru originally gave him a Sanskrit term that didn't click, so he substituted this simpler word) for the element that decides a person's foundational spiritual/karmic standing — shaping physical form, attraction, speech, wealth, status, and how much weight one's voice carries.

Q4. How does the classical seven-chakra system r elate to Dimension? A: Per this teaching, beyond the well-known seven chakras lie seven more (14 total); crossing all 14 and passing beyond a kind of astral "sky" constitutes the first Dimension, with the next Dimension directly after being the 32-chakra Dimension. Chakras are like stairs; Dimensions are like floors.

Q5. If I r each a new Dimension, does that make me powerful ther e automatically? A: No — per this teaching, each floor (Dimension) already has many subtle bodies residing there who must also be "crossed"; reaching a floor doesn't make you its ruler .

Q6. Does someone need to be r eligious or devoted to have a Dimension? A: No — this teaching states every human being has a Dimension, devotee or not, because physical-world Dimension and astral-world Dimension are separate tracks; someone with a strong astral Dimension can behave like royalty in the unseen world with no conscious spiritual practice at all.

Q7. Is ther e an actual scale used to measur e Dimension? A: Yes — this teaching describes a numeric scale given by Bhaiya's guru specifically for this purpose, similar to how scientists use light-years for planets; on it, ordinary people commonly range from roughly 500 up to 5,000-8,000.

Q8. Why did Bhaiya's own Dimension fall to zer o and then negative? A: Per this teaching, unresolved anger and jealousy directed at his father and mother by others was, in ef fect, dischar ged onto Bhaiya as a child — displaced family negativity landing on the next generation without any personal wrongdoing involved, compounded by sustained tantric attacks against him.

Q9. What is Dimension's cor e function according to Bhaiya's guru? A: Bhaiya's guru's core teaching states Dimension is "the link that connects one birth to the next" — deciding what a person becomes, which birth they take, and how life unfolds; it is the exact chart devtas use to judge a person's standing.

Q10. Can someone simply r each a comfortable Dimension level and stop working on it? A: No — this teaching is explicit that no one can remain static on any Dimension; subtly-stationed beings already at that level will contest and pull down anyone who stops advancing, so a person either keeps climbing or begins falling from wherever they stopped.

Q1 1. Who actually has the power to lower a person's Dimension — devtas, or other humans? A: Per this teaching, only another human being can lower (or help raise) a human's Dimension; Bhagwan and devtas never interfere with a person's Dimension at all, a point Bhaiya says genuinely shocked him when he first learned it.

Q12. What ar e the two br oad ways to raise one's Dimension? A: Physical means (yoga, exercise, surya namaskar , pranic healing, quality food and possessions — this teaching notes even objects like phones carry their own Dimension) and astral means (dhyan, tap, and mantra jaap).

Q13. If my mantra is alr eady powerful, do I still need to worry about my own personal Dimension? A: Yes — per this teaching, mantra Dimension and personal Dimension are related but separate tracks; even a hugely jagrit mantra (which can protect a practitioner independent of their own Dimension) does not substitute for the personal Dimension needed for genuine recognition and standing among fellow humans.

Q14. How did Bhaiya's own mantra pr otect him even while his personal Dimension was in the negative? A: This teaching states his mantra shakti was already jagrit (awakened) from the start, sitting in the "kharabs" (hundreds of billions) even while his personal Dimension was at zero or negative — which is why 33 tantriks who attacked him over the years all found their siddhis rendered inef fective, since they were contending with his mantra's Dimension, not his personal one.

Q15. Can Dimension rise thr ough discipline alone, without any devotional practice? A: Yes, but per this teaching each purely disciplined, non-devotional practice (punctuality , a fixed sleep schedule, healthy eating) has its own fixed ceiling it cannot exceed, no matter how long it's sustained — illustrated by contrasting a highly disciplined public figure's capped Dimension against someone anchored to an external devotional shakti, who is not bound by that same ceiling.

Q16. What's the caution illustrated by the Akshay Kumar anecdote about visiting Vaishno Devi? A: Per this teaching, reasoning that devotional spending (travel, of ferings) would be better redirected to more "practical" purposes corresponded to an actual Dimension loss — illustrating that rationalizing away devotional practice for sensible-sounding practical reasons carries a real spiritual cost.

Q17. Who holds the highest Dimension of all, according to this teaching? A: Mahadev (Shiva) — and since Dimension applies specifically to humans (Bhagwan Ram is explicitly placed outside this framework), the implication is that Mahadev himself was, at some point, human.

Q18. Does Bhaiya's own guru, Hanuman Ji Maharaj, also have a Dimension? A: Yes — per this teaching, vastly smaller than Mahadev's but still enormous; because a guru already possesses a lar ge Dimension, that guru can carry a devoted disciple upward.

Q19. What's the biggest risk of making a living human being your guru? A: Per this teaching, your own Dimension can never exceed that guru's while they remain your guru — and if that guru's Dimension ever falls (through a tantric attack, moral failing, or losing sanity), yours falls with it, since they are responsible for raising you.

Q20. What kind of guru avoids this risk? A: A guru who has taken "Jeevit Samadhi" (living samadhi) and is thus fully , permanently jagrit — such beings (Neem Karoli Baba is given as an example) continue growing their own Dimension without limit, unlike an ordinary human teacher whose Dimension is bound to their fallible mortal state.

Q21. What alternative does Bhaiya suggest instead of making an ordinary person your formal guru? A: Treating each other as brothers/companions in devotion — walking the path together and praying for one another — rather than entering a binding gurudisciple relationship with its associated risk.

Q22. Would Hanuman Ji Maharaj ever take sides if two devotees of his got into a Dimension-based conflict? A: No — per this teaching, devtas never intervene in Dimension disputes between two devotees of the same deity , even hypothetically between two wellknown dhams; such disputes are purely human matters of tapobal, mantra shakti, tap shakti, and kundli shakti.

Q23. If devtas stay out of Dimension conflicts, how does prayer to my guru actually help me when I'm attacked? A: Per this teaching, a guru's own tatva is present at every Dimension level below the guru's own maximum, so sincere prayer can activate that guru's subtle presence at the exact level of an attacker — but only as far as the guru's own Dimension genuinely reaches, which is why a low-Dimension human guru limits how much protection is actually available.

Q24. In the "Anshu" household example, why couldn't the tantric attack succeed against either Anshu or his unawar e mother? A: Because Anshu had, knowingly or not, granted his mother a form of blessing/shakti that now stood behind her daily ritual regardless of her own awareness; per this teaching, that made any outside attack against either of them "null and void," since Anshu is protected by his own shakti and his mother acted only out of unaware devotion, not malicious intent.

Q25. If such attacks ar e rendered null and void, what's the r eal fix in a case like Anshu's? A: The tar geted person must raise their own personal Dimension, so that repeating rituals or cycles built around them permanently lose their capacity to af fect them at all.

Q26. Why does Ashaeiynn hold a monthly Mahayagya specifically? A: It took Bhaiya roughly a year to understand that people connected to Ashaeiynn who cannot raise their own Dimension through personal ef fort alone need dedicated collective help — Mahayagya's specific sankalp works directly on raising participants' Dimension, roughly 50 to 500 points per session.

Q27. What is the "Raksha Suraksha" sankalp, and how is it differ ent from the Jagriti sankalp? A: Raksha Suraksha is a separate, ongoing sankalp for people whose devotional practice is being actively obstructed by someone close to them; raising Dimension through it ef fectively brings the obstructing party "below" the practitioner so they become receptive, whereas the Jagriti sankalp performed at Mahayagya is specifically about raising bhakti-based Dimension itself.

Q28. Does putting in mor e jaap hours simply add up Dimension gains in a straight line? A: No — per this teaching, gains compound exponentially rather than adding linearly , because each practice session also grows the practitioner's own mantra shakti, which carries its own (much lar ger) Dimension that compounds together with personal gains across repeated sessions.

Q29. Why have Ashaeiynn's ten Mahayagyas over ten months pr oduced Dimension gains that seem to exceed simple math? A: Because each Mahayagya not only grants a direct 50–500 point gift but also strengthens participants' ongoing mantra shakti and their bond with fellow sadhaks, so later sessions build on genuinely compounded prior gains rather than starting fresh — producing results well beyond a naive linear estimate.

Q30. If Mahayagya's cor e sankalps ar e Jagriti and Raksha Suraksha, why do r egistration slots still list pitru and negativity hawan categories? A: Per this teaching, daily hawans already handle pitru and negativity in smaller , routine doses; on Mahayagya day , the much lar ger quantity of bhog of fered draws a correspondingly lar ger number of saints and mahatmas, compressing roughly ten days' worth of ordinary pitru/negativity clearing into that single day .
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 50 additions)

Keep "Dimension" ( डायमेंशन) precisely distinct from "mantra Dimension" — the teaching treats these as related but separate tracks, and answers should never conflate a practitioner's own standing with their mantra's independently jagrit power . Present the "only humans lower/raise a human's Dimension, never devtas or Bhagwan" rule as this teaching's own stated framework, without extending it into a broader claim about divine non-intervention in other contexts (e.g., pitru or negativity matters covered in other sessions). Handle questions about making a human being one's guru with real care and nuance — this teaching's caution (Dimension capped at the guru's own, and falling if the guru's falls) is specific guidance from this session, not a blanket condemnation of all

human-guru relationships in general spiritual life. When explaining the Akshay Kumar/V aishno Devi anecdote or any other named public figure example, frame it strictly as this teaching's own illustrative case study , not as a factual claim about that person's real spiritual state. Preserve the "exponential/compounding, not linear" explanation for Dimension gains precisely as presented — avoid restating it as a simple flat per -session number . Keep the "devtas never fight over Dimension disputes" rule scoped to Dimension-related conflicts specifically , consistent with this teaching's own framing. Distinguish the Jagriti/Dimension-raising Mahayagya sankalp clearly from the separate Raksha Suraksha sankalp when answering questions about Ashaeiynn's rituals.
